#### MATERIAL — F1

> so the default route installs nothing and the workflow is otherwise identical
- **Question**: How do ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN reach the pipeline step's environment? The design's only workflow changes are the job-level AGENT_BACKEND env and the gated install step (D11), and the Migration Plan says a repository merely 'sets AGENT_BACKEND=claude at job level and exactly one Anthropic secret' — but a GitHub repository secret never enters a step's env unless the workflow forwards it. Today every credential is forwarded line-by-line (LLM_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.LLM_API_KEY }}, etc.); without equivalent new forwarding lines the D5 guard always sees neither-set and every claude-route job fails at startup. The artifacts must state the forwarding lines (and ideally that workflow.test.ts pins them, not just 'the gate and the version's exactness').
- **Code evidence**: Read .github/workflows/agent-pipeline.yml: the 'Run the agent pipeline' step maps each credential explicitly from secrets/vars (LLM_API_KEY, LLM_BASE_URL, LLM_MODEL, AGENT_MCP_SERVERS via secrets.AGENT_MCP_SERVERS || vars..., AGENT_LOG_KEY); GitHub Actions injects no repository secret implicitly. opencode-agent/src/index.ts:201 — loadConfig(options.env, args.repoRoot) reads the guard's variables from that step env; index.ts:198-201 — config loads before the logger, matching D5's 'ahead of the logger'. Searched all three artifacts for any mention of forwarding the Anthropic spellings into the step env: none exists; D11 claims 'the workflow is otherwise identical' and the spec's install requirement likewise says 'Nothing else in the workflow, the phase cascade or the state machine SHALL differ between the two backends', which an implementer could read as forbidding the needed env lines.
- **Resolution**: edited — design.md D11 now specifies the credential forwarding: the pipeline step gains ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN lines gated on AGENT_BACKEND == 'claude' (GitHub injects no repository secret implicitly — agent-pipeline.yml:458 forwards LLM_API_KEY line-by-line today, so without new lines the guard would always see neither-set), LLM_API_KEY / LLM_BASE_URL gain the inverse gate, model knobs stay forwarded on both routes; workflow.test.ts pins the forwarding gates beside the install gate and version exactness; the spec's workflow requirement and a new 'Credentials are forwarded only to their own backend' scenario back it, and the Migration Plan notes the merged workflow already forwards route-gated.

#### MATERIAL — F2

> The job's configured model and the invoking profile's reasoning effort SHALL be passed explicitly as `--model` and `--effort` on every invocation
- **Question**: What `--effort` does a spawn carry when the profile's effort knob is unset, or when the profile is `propose`? The spec's determinism requirement and its 'Every spawn carries the determinism and model flags' scenario assert an explicit `--effort` on every invocation, but design D3 says effort 'is omitted when unset' and that `propose` 'gets none, matching its empty variant on the OpenCode side'. Under the ordinary configuration (effort knobs unset — the workflow forwards them through unset by default) and on every propose turn, the design's spawn violates the spec scenario as written; conversely, always passing `--effort` would force inventing a value no knob supplies. Either the spec softens to 'when the invoking profile has an effort configured' or the design must state propose/unset behavior as spec-compliant.
- **Code evidence**: opencode-agent/src/config.ts:92-96 — profiles read only LLM_MODEL_LIGHT, AGENT_EFFORT_PLAN and AGENT_EFFORT_BUILD via effortTier (null when unset); grep over opencode-agent/src finds no effort knob for propose anywhere. opencode-agent/src/phases/plan-draft.ts:163 — live caller prompting with agent: 'propose', so propose spawns are real. opencode-agent/src/openai-config.ts:271-272 — the weaker-profile/unset-emits-nothing doctrine the design cites. agent-pipeline.yml forwards AGENT_EFFORT_PLAN/AGENT_EFFORT_BUILD from vars, which are unset by default, so the conflict is the common case, not an edge.
- **Resolution**: edited — The spec's determinism requirement was the outlier: it now demands --model explicitly on every invocation but --effort 'whenever that profile has an effort configured', with the omit-when-unset / propose-gets-none behavior stated as the compliant case, and the 'Every spawn carries the determinism and model flags' scenario softened to match. The design (D3) was left unchanged — it matches the repo doctrine (config.ts:94-95 reads the effort knobs as optional-null effortTier; openai-config.ts gives propose an empty variant). Duplicate of the second reviewer set's F1; same edit resolves both.

- **Question**: Does the wrap-up prompt that follows a deadline-killed turn resume the killed turn's session, or start a fresh one? D1's 'successful' gating and D7/spec's unconditional chaining give opposite answers, and the killed-turn wrap-up is a load-bearing above-the-seam behavior.

#### MATERIAL — F1

> `close()` is never a stop and never a fallback for a refused kill: it reaps what remains and best-effort removes the job-scoped config dir.
- **Question**: What does close() do with a CLI child that is still RUNNING at teardown? A turn deadline fired outside the implement phase (plan/triage/answer/ci-fix/plan-draft/sync all prompt without turn-stop), or a mid-turn crash, leaves the spawned CLI alive: 'reaps what remains' is undefined for a live child — waiting for it blocks teardown past AGENT_TEARDOWN_RESERVE_MS (the report may never post), abandoning it leaves a live, credentialed, detached (own process group) model process running past the run's end, which is exactly the leak class the design's own goal bullet ('fix, on this route, the orphan leak close() has on the OpenCode side') claims to close — on the OpenCode route close() SIGTERMs the server pid so the model process dies at teardown, while this route's close() kills nothing by its own words. Neither the design (D8) nor the spec's stop requirement ('Teardown (close) SHALL only reap what remains and SHALL NOT be used as a stop') states this path, and no risk bullet records it.
- **Code evidence**: Answered from the repo as far as it goes: index.ts:117-125 — teardown is only `await agent.close(); await proxy.close(); await transcript?.close()`, no abort anywhere; rg confirms the sole aborter is turn-stop, imported only by phases/implement.ts:15 (stopPartWayThrough), so every other prompting phase (triage.ts:113, plan.ts, plan-draft.ts:163, answer.ts:40, intent.ts:58, ci-fix.ts, sync.ts:191, turn-stop.ts:243 itself) reaches teardown with the child possibly still running after a deadline; on the OpenCode route connection.close() kills the spawned server (CLAUDE.md: 'close() — which on POSIX is one proc.kill() on one pid'), so the asymmetry is real, not assumed. The artifacts' wording is the only place the live-child-at-close case could be answered, and it is silent — the residual is bounded in CI only by runner VM teardown, and unbounded on local --event-path runs.
- **Resolution**: edited — Design D8 and the spec's stop requirement amended. D8 now states that close() finding a live CLI group at teardown (a deadline-abandoned turn outside the implement phase — turn-stop is the pipeline's sole aborter and index.ts:118-124 calls only agent.close() — or a crashed run) delivers the same SIGTERM→grace→SIGKILL group escalation fire-and-forget (grace timer never blocks process exit or AGENT_TEARDOWN_RESERVE_MS), then reaps and removes the job-scoped config dir; waiting would hang teardown past the reserve and lose the report. The spec requirement is reworded from 'teardown SHALL only reap' to 'SHALL NOT be used as a turn's stop or as the fallback for a kill that did not land; a CLI process still alive at teardown SHALL be terminated with the same group-kill mechanism, fire-and-forget', with a new scenario 'An abandoned child is terminated at teardown'. This matches the OpenCode route, whose close() kills the server pid (opencode-connect.ts:131), keeping the route's own goal — closing the orphan leak — true; the second-set MCP finding is F1b.

- **Resolution**: edited — Design D1 no longer claims the init line always precedes a kill. It now says --resume carries the memoized id 'whenever one is memoized' — normally even for a killed turn, since the init line is the stream's first line — and names the edge: a kill during CLI startup, before any line arrived, memoizes nothing; the next turn spawns without --resume into a fresh session (no context exists to fork — the killed turn produced none), and a wrap-up asked in that state lands in that fresh session and reports what it can.
